title_en: Wu Jiwei v. Nanjing Bofeng Electric Tools Co., Ltd. — labor contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: Whether an overall relocation of the employer resulting in a change of the worker's workplace and an extension of commute time falls under the circumstance of 'a major change in objective circumstances upon which the labor contract was concluded, rendering the labor contract unperformable' as provided in Article 40(3) of the Labor Contract Law of the PRC requires a comprehensive assessment of the relocation distance, convenience of commuting, and whether the employer has provided transportation, adjusted work attendance hours, or increased transportation subsidies, in order to determine whether the change of workplace has caused severe inconvenience to the worker's work and life and is sufficient to affect the performance of the labor contract. If the employer has taken appropriate measures to mitigate the adverse impact of the relocation on the worker, and the relocation is not sufficient to render the labor contract unperformable, the worker shall not refuse to provide labor on that ground.

full_text_en:
Wu Jiwei v. Nanjing Bofeng Electric Tool Co., Ltd. — labor contract dispute

【Ruling Summary】

Whether a relocation of the employer's entire workplace resulting in a change of the worker's work location and an extension of commuting time falls within the circumstances set forth in Article 40(3) of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China – namely, "a major change in the objective circumstances relied upon at the time of conclusion of the labor contract, rendering the contract impossible to perform" – requires a comprehensive assessment of factors such as the distance of the relocation, commuting convenience, and whether the employer has provided transportation, adjusted work schedules, or increased transportation subsidies, to evaluate whether the change in work location causes serious inconvenience to the worker's work and life sufficient to affect performance of the labor contract. If the employer has taken appropriate measures to mitigate the adverse effects of the relocation on the worker, and the relocation itself does not render the labor contract impossible to perform, the worker may not refuse to provide labor on that ground.

Plaintiff: Wu Jiwei, male, born October 6, 1990, Han Chinese, residing in Mingguang City, Anhui Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Bofeng Electric Tool Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Lennart de Vet, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Plaintiff Wu Jiwei filed an action with the People's Court of Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone, Jiangsu Province, against Defendant Nanjing Bofeng Electric Tool Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bofeng Company) concerning a labor contract dispute.

Plaintiff Wu Jiwei alleged: He was formerly an employee of Defendant Bofeng Company. On March 9, 2019, Bofeng Company unilaterally relocated without prior notice, and later directly issued a notice of termination of the labor contract on March 18. Wu Jiwei now demanded that Bofeng Company pay compensation of RMB 57,192.

Defendant Bofeng Company argued: Due to production and operational needs and to improve the working environment, it decided to relocate from No. 159 Jiangjun Avenue to No. 529 Jiangjun Avenue in April 2019. On March 9, 2019, while organizing employees to dismantle a production line with no tasks, over 100 employees, including Plaintiff Wu Jiwei, collectively stopped work. The company invited government departments to provide legal explanations and announced that welfare benefits would remain unchanged, and an additional monthly transportation subsidy of RMB 50 would be issued, calling on employees to return to work, but the employees continued to cease work. The company thereafter repeatedly notified employees to return to work, warning that otherwise they would be dismissed in accordance with the company's rules and regulations, but all were refused. Wu Jiwei seriously violated the company's rules and regulations and the most basic labor discipline, and thus the company's termination of the labor contract was lawful.

The People's Court of Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone found at first instance:

On September 23, 2013, Plaintiff Wu Jiwei joined Defendant Bofeng Company to engage in production work. The last term of the labor contract between the parties was executed until September 30, 2019, stipulating that the work location was at No. 159 Jiangjun Avenue (Bofeng Company premises), and that any change to provisions or material matters directly affecting the worker's interests should be agreed upon through consultation.

On May 4, 2017, Defendant Bofeng Company held a workers' congress to review and amend the employee handbook. Among other provisions, it stipulated that continuous absence from work for three working days, or cumulative absence from work for five working days within a consecutive 12-month period, would result in termination of the contract. Plaintiff Wu Jiwei signed to acknowledge receipt of the employee handbook.

In March 2019, due to operational needs, Defendant Bofeng Company decided to relocate its entire premises from No. 159 Jiangjun Avenue to No. 529 Jiangjun Avenue. After learning of this, employees including Plaintiff Wu Jiwei refused to report to the new factory site, citing excessive distance. On March 9, 2019, when Bofeng Company organized personnel to dismantle the production line, a large number of employees, including Wu Jiwei, engaged in a work stoppage. From that day forward, they clocked in at the original factory site each day but did not provide labor thereafter. On March 11, 2019, Bofeng Company issued a notice on the factory relocation, stating that effective April 1, 2019, the factory site would be relocated entirely from No. 159 Jiangjun Avenue (14,000 square meters) to No. 529 Jiangjun Avenue (17,000 square meters), a distance of approximately 4.5 kilometers, a journey of about 20 minutes by bicycle, both locations along Metro Line S1, accessible by buses 864 and 874, the production workshop would be equipped with central air conditioning, and dining and accommodation would be more convenient. Bofeng Company would arrange vehicles to take all employees to visit the new factory, grant each person a relocation bonus of RMB 500, and increase the monthly transportation subsidy from RMB 100 by an additional RMB 50, asking employees to communicate through reasonable channels and to return to work normally by 8:30 a.m. on March 12, 2019. The employees refused to return to work. On March 13, 2019, Bofeng Company issued another announcement, reiterating that employees' positions, work content, and welfare benefits remained unchanged, and that the additional RMB 50 transportation subsidy would be granted. The employees still refused to return to work. On March 15, 2019, Bofeng Company issued a notice urging Wu Jiwei to return to work, informing him that his conduct had seriously violated the company's rules and regulations, disrupting and undermining production order, and requiring him to report to the production supervisor by 8:30 a.m. on March 18, 2019, failing which the labor contract would be terminated. Wu Jiwei did not report as required. On March 18, 2019, after notifying the trade union, Bofeng Company decided to terminate the labor contract with Wu Jiwei on the ground of serious violation of the company's rules and regulations.

On March 25, 2019, Plaintiff Wu Jiwei filed a claim with the Nanjing Jiangning District Labor Dispute Arbitration Commission, with the same arbitration requests as in this lawsuit. On May 6, 2019, the arbitration commission issued an award dismissing Wu Jiwei's arbitration claims. Defendant Bofeng Company accepted the award. Wu Jiwei, dissatisfied with the award, filed this lawsuit.

The People's Court of Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone held at first instance:

Defendant Bofeng Company's proposed relocation of its entire factory was a business decision made based on production and operational circumstances, which did not change the workers' positions or benefits, and was not an abuse of the right to employ workers designed to deliberately make things difficult for them. The relocation of the factory might indeed impose some commuting pressure on workers, but the relocation distance was not great, and the new location was accessible by public transportation and shared bicycles. Jiangjun Avenue itself had good traffic conditions, and Bofeng Company had also promised to increase the transportation subsidy. Overall, the impact of the relocation on workers was limited and did not constitute a fundamental obstacle to the continued performance of the labor contract between the parties. At the same time, after the dispute arose, both parties should have taken proper measures to protect their respective rights. Plaintiff Wu Jiwei, who was unwilling to adjust to the changed work location, could have raised relevant demands, but he still bore the obligation to continue to comply with the company's rules and regulations and to continue to perform the labor contract. Despite repeated notices from Bofeng Company, Wu Jiwei still refused to return to his original position, which constituted absenteeism, violated basic labor discipline, and reached the severity level stipulated in the employee handbook for termination of the labor contract. Therefore, Bofeng Company's decision to terminate the labor contract after notifying the trade union was not unlawful. Accordingly, Wu Jiwei's request for Bofeng Company to pay compensation for unlawful termination of the labor contract was not supported.

In conclusion, the People's Court of Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone, in accordance with Article 39(2) of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on October 8, 2019:

All of Plaintiff Wu Jiwei's claims are dismissed.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, neither party appealed, and the judgment of first instance has taken legal effect.
